messages:
ops-bot: [ALERT] Canary SLO breach: canary-omega p95=1.9s (>1.2s), error-rate jump. Pager fired to #incidents.

maya: oncall here, i'm looking into it now. tagging eng.

devin: noticing 502/5xx around the canary slice, matches canary-omega. @samir can you confirm routing?

samir: canary-omega pinned to model:v2-quant. pulling logs and KV cache metrics.

samir: logs show repeated cache miss spikes + slow quant kernels: `ERROR serve.go: cache_miss=true latency_ms=2050 req=xyz`

maya: can we flip the feature flag for just that canary? need emergency rollback.

devin: flag is `features.rollout.model-v2`. we support per-canary scope. command to run: `ffctl set features.rollout.model-v2 false --scope=canary-omega`

maya: executing now.

ops-bot: Feature flag update: features.rollout.model-v2=false for canary-omega (actor: maya).

adrian: recommend traffic siphon to stable-v1 and graceful drain of canary. run: `infractl traffic shift --from canary-omega --to stable-v1 --percent 100` when ready.

samir: starting traffic siphon + warming stable cache. initiating KV prefill on stable nodes.

ops-bot: TrafficShift job started (id ts-20240317-omega). est finish ~75s.

liz: Support: multiple customers opened tickets describing truncated or malformed outputs ~11:07UTC. attaching examples.

maya: acknowledged. assigning customer comms: @liz please prepare a short note.

devin: running quick smoke tests post-shift:
```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood-inference/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"Hi","max_tokens":10}' | jq -r .text
```

devin: smoke: stable-v1 responses OK (p95 ~420ms), no malformed outputs in 10 samples.

samir: root cause hypothesis: v2-quant canary config used 64MB KV cache (override) vs 256MB on stable -> thrashing with quant kernels -> latency + errors.

ops-bot: TrafficShift job ts-20240317-omega completed. canary-omega drained.

maya: incident mitigated. switching to postmortem flow. handing active investigation to eng.

liz: customer note draft: "We experienced degraded responses during a limited canary rollout of an optimization. We rolled back the canary and service has returned to normal. Engineering is investigating and will follow up."

adrian: scheduling follow-up with infra+ml-ops to fix default cache size, add canary preflight with cache checks, and add a canary-level flag safety timeout.

maya: oncall declares stabilized. will stay available for followups but handing off.

ops-bot: Incident state -> mitigated; assigned inc id: inc-20240317-omega; status: postmortem_pending."
